title: The music falls out of time in play: a long burst takes the stems' voices away and each stem starts again from its top at its own moment
evidence: Measured on the recordings of the final gate, brought to this machine and analysed with numpy (each stem's place in its 20.87 s loop by cross-correlation with the stem's own file; scripts /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MURDER-INC-/143426e3-80dd-56d9-8134-6c37a8961002/scratchpad/rev3b/phase.py, phase2.py, stems.py). SHIPPING game of the zip aa7cc478 (box: /project/ue/cloud/lag/snd-keys/sound.wav): before the magazine is emptied (10 to 52 s) drums 16.660 s, bass 16.657, keys 16.660, crackle 16.660: together within 3 ms. The 30 rounds are fired from 67.0 to 70.2 s; the drum stem is last matched in its old place up to 67.4 s and begins again from its first sample at 69.69 s. From there to the end of the run: drums 7.080, crackle 7.144 (+64 ms), bass 7.291 (+211 ms, the same in three separate windows, correlation 0.45 to 0.55 against 0.27 to 0.40 for the next best place), hats 7.400 (+320 ms). DEVELOPMENT game (snd-dev): all five within 3 ms at 16.613 until the demo's magazine dump at 12:18:41 to 12:18:44 (the game's log: 49, 88 and 87 sound starts a second, 72 one-shot sounds alive at once by their lengths); the drums begin again at 76.34 s of the recording (12:18:43.9); afterwards bass +190 ms from the drums (two windows), and in the fight (140 to 186 s) keys +298 ms, strings and bell both at 4.425 s while the drums are at 13.732 (9.3 s apart = 3.57 bars). In snd-free and snd-l35 (a burst of 1.2 s) the drums keep their place. Cause, read in the engine on the box (not confirmed by an engine log: no game may be started now): the audio device has 32 voices (FAudioQualitySettings::MaxChannels(32), Engine/Classes/Sound/AudioSettings.h:93; game log 'AudioDevice MaxSources: 32'; Config/DefaultEngine.ini has no audio section). GetSortedActiveWaveInstances sorts by volume x priority, only the loudest 32 keep a voice and StopSources stops the rest (Engine/Private/AudioDevice.cpp:4282-4327, 4491-4530). Every component is created with the default priority (MIAudioSubsystem.cpp:386; the director's C.Priority is never passed on) and under gunfire the stems play at 0.02 to 0.13 (0.4 x the 0.45 duck), so they go first. A looping wave that lost its voice, or whose volume is 0, starts from its first sample when it comes back (SoundBase.cpp:15 VirtualizationMode(Restart), SoundBase.h:57-77; Audio.cpp:1134). Strings and bell are at exactly 0 from the first frame (MIAudioDirector.cpp:964-977). The director's own limit per sound stops one voice per shot while it starts up to three (MIAudioDirector.cpp:331-356). The web game: seven stems of exactly eight bars that loop side by side without drifting (src/audio/music.js:1-2), a late stem joins at the right offset (src/audio/conductor.js:1-2); 92 BPM, a sixteenth note is 163 ms.
failure: Every player who holds the trigger through a magazine (three seconds, the first thing anyone does with the CHOPPER) loses the music for those seconds and gets it back with the bass a fifth of a second and the hats a third of a second behind the drums, for the rest of the session; the strings and the bell of every big fight come in off the beat and on the wrong bar; Hold the Block (up to 30 enemies) will do it constantly. By the same rule the quietest one-shots (far enemies, impacts, cases) lose their voices in those seconds. It is in both games of the zip to upload. The report's 'the music has no gap' looks only for digital silence in the stream and its own list of drum loop starts (16.7, 37.5, 69.7, 90.6, 111.4 s) already shows the jump; nothing in sound-gate.txt looks at the music's time.
fix: (1) Config/DefaultEngine.ini: [/Script/Engine.AudioSettings] +QualityLevels=(DisplayName=NSLOCTEXT("AudioSettings","DefaultSettingsName","Default"),MaxChannels=96) (the web pools add up to 89: audio.json categories.voices); the log must then say 'Max Channels (voices): 96'. (2) Stems and beds keep a voice and keep time: in mi_audio_import.py set virtualization_mode to PLAY_WHEN_SILENT on the looping waves (or W->VirtualizationMode = EVirtualizationMode::PlayWhenSilent beside W->bLooping = true in Execute), and in Execute A->bAlwaysPlay = true for the categories music and ambience and A->Priority from C.Priority for the rest. (3) Let the director's Max stop as many old voices as a Play starts. (4) Put the check into the gate: after 'empty' in sound-keys.txt and after the fight of sound-demo.txt every stem's loop phase must equal the drums' and be what it was on the home screen; an automation test that the seven stems are PlayWhenSilent. To confirm the cause before building, the Development game of the present zip can be started with the launch option -ini:Engine:[/Script/Engine.AudioSettings]:QualityLevels=(MaxChannels=96) and the drums' phase read through the magazine dump. Needs a build, a package and both gates.

title: Goon footsteps play inside the player's head: 2D, at the level of the player's own steps, whatever the distance
evidence: StartFile makes a sound 3D only when its own category is world or ambience (MIAudioDirector.cpp:265: C.b3D = Args.b3D && (Def.Category == world || ambience)) and keeps the definition's category. The Goon step asks for 3D at the Goon's place (lines 876-882) with step_asphalt_run, whose bus is 'near' (audio_sounds.json), so it comes out 2D in the category near. The game's own log of the final Development run (/project/ue/cloud/lag/snd-dev/game.log): 356 'play ... sound=step_asphalt_run category=Near' lines, none with ' 3d'; 300 of them (150 steps, pitch 0.83 to 0.93) are the Goons', at volume 0.287 (web layer) and 0.539 (Gen layer) against 0.309 and 0.579 for the player's own sprint; up to 16 Goon steps a second (12:20:25); they are a quarter of all 1,148 sounds the run started. The web game plays them on the world bus at the Goon's position with distance: A.play(stepName(p.surface, true), { pos: p.pos, bus: 'world', volume: 0.75, pitch: 0.88, ref: 3, roll: 1.2 }) (src/audio/react.js:228-231; src/audio.js:356-393; src/enemies/goon.js:994): at 20 m that is 0.13 of the level (-18 dB), at 40 m 0.06.
failure: In every fight the player hears a crowd running at his own feet, with no direction and no distance, 5 to 24 dB louder than the web game has it, whenever a Goon moves within 45 m; the steps also take voices from the 32 the engine has (finding 1) and share the three-voice limit of the player's own steps. The report's table counts these as 'the demo's walks' (step_asphalt_run 16 of 24).
fix: Give FPlayArgs a category and a distance law of its own (FName Category; double Ref, Roll), let StartFile use them (C.Category = Args.Category.IsNone() ? Def.Category : Args.Category; the 3D rule on C.Category; Ref and Roll from the arguments when set; the same category in the Live entry), and set them for the Goon step: world, ref 3 m, roll 1.2 (audio.json goonSteps: "category": "world", "ref": 3.0, "roll": 1.2). New automation test: a tracked Goon that runs 1.6 m within 45 m gives a Start command that is 3D, category world, at the Goon's position. Then the Development run again: the log lines must end in ' 3d'.

title: Every measurement was of a mono stream: where a sound comes from was never observed, and what E3DS's page asks for is unknown
evidence: The game's log in the final Development run (snd-dev/game.log line 1666): 'EncoderInbuiltWrapper. In-built audio encoder has been successfully created. codec=[Opus] ... numChannels=[1]'. In all four recordings I checked (snd-keys, snd-dev, snd-free, snd-l35) left minus right is digital zero (side level -270 dB, correlation 1.000), also in the Development run with over 400 starts marked '3d' and the stereo street bed. The viewer answers the game's offer with aiortc's plain answer (rtcinput.py:285-287), which has no stereo=1 for Opus; a WebRTC sender then encodes one channel. The game itself hands two channels to the sender (Engine/Plugins/Media/PixelStreaming2/Source/PixelStreaming2RTC/Private/EpicRtcStreamer.cpp:1510-1513, _channels = 2) after folding its six (PixelStreaming2/Internal/UtilsAudio.h:69-79). E3DS's documentation says nothing about stereo. AUDIO.md section 9 says the stream carries two channels; that is not what was measured.
failure: If E3DS's page asks for stereo, players get a mix nobody measured: by the engine's numbers a 2D mono sound is at half amplitude in each ear and the stereo street bed at full, so the bed is 6 dB (not the 3 dB of the report, which is what a mono fold shows) over guns, voice and music, and 3D sounds lie between. If it does not, players get one channel and cannot tell by ear where a Goon or a Buzzard is, which the web game gives them. Either way the report's 'proven through a real WebRTC stream' does not cover direction or the stereo balance.
fix: In rtcinput.py add stereo=1;sprop-stereo=1 to the Opus fmtp line of the answer before it is sent (what Epic's own player page does); let rtcaudio.py print the side level and say MONO when it is digital zero; run snd-dev and snd-keys again and check that a sound marked 3d leans to one side and what the bed's level is against a gun. Read once what E3DS's page answers (the first session with sound: the page's WebRTC statistics, or ask the owner whether a Buzzard on the left sounds left) and put the result into AUDIO.md 9 and LAUNCH.md.

title: Every 2D sound is at half amplitude: the engine's default mono upmix, one line of config away from the web game's convention
evidence: Measured by the sound engineer and reproduced here: every mono sound arrives 4.5 to 6.5 dB under volume x category gain (my re-run of sound_table.py on snd-dev gives the same table: 174 of 396 found, 44 ms). The cause is a project setting left at its default: UAudioSettings::MonoChannelUpmixMethod, first value Linear = 'the mono channel is split 0.5 left/right' (Engine/Classes/Sound/AudioSettings.h:42-52, 241; applied in AudioMixer/Private/AudioMixerChannelMaps.cpp:97-109; the constructor in Engine/Private/AudioSettings.cpp:20-33 sets neither it nor PanningMethod; the project's Config has no audio section). The web game plays a mono buffer at full level in both channels and pans 3D sounds with equal power. Result in the stream: home screen -28 dBFS RMS, a run at rest -27 dBFS, and the master chain (compressor at -6 dB) driven about 6 dB less than it was designed for.
failure: The whole game is quiet against anything else a browser plays, the street bed (and in a stereo stream every 3D sound at the side) is 3 to 6 dB too loud against guns, voice and music, and the compressor that glues the web mix hardly works. Not silent and not clipping, but not the mix the data describes.
fix: A decision for the lead, to take with the build that finding 1 needs anyway: [/Script/Engine.AudioSettings] MonoChannelUpmixMethod=FullVolume and PanningMethod=EqualPower in Config/DefaultEngine.ini (the same section as MaxChannels), then the mix part of the sound gate again: peaks (the limiter now works as on the web), the level of each part, the bed against a gun. If it is left as it is, AUDIO.md should name the setting as the cause and say 6 dB for a stereo listener.

title: The package guard checks names only: a Sound Wave with no audio in it, or an old cook, passes every check and the game counts it as played
evidence: pak_sounds.py asks only whether MurderInc/Content/Audio/<name>.uasset is in Manifest_UFSFiles_Linux.txt. The audio itself is in the .ubulk (build of 10:48: chopper_shot_01.uasset 814 bytes, .uexp 130, .ubulk 3,809; ui_hover_01.ubulk 415), the cook runs with -IgnoreCookErrors (package-cloud.sh:181), and the game adds to sndPlayed after A->Play() whatever the wave holds (MIAudioSubsystem.cpp:405), so a wave whose audio failed to encode is 'in the pak', 'started' and silent, with sndMissing=0. The tests' check (Duration > 0.01, SoundsResolve) is of the editor's asset in the gameplay clone, not of the cook. Staleness: the content step returns 'CONTENT KEPT' before its own missing-or-older check when any UnrealEditor has the gameplay clone open, a test run included (lines 86-91); 'package Shipping' skips the cook whenever Saved/Cooked exists (line 182), so content, package Shipping, zip ships the audio of the older cook with 'SOUNDS OK'; the older-than test is by file time, which cp -p or tar keep. sync.sh and the content step say nothing when Content/Audio/Web is absent but Gen and Voice are imported (the count is 0 0 and the function returns before its Web check); only the cook's end or SoundsResolve then says so.
failure: A package that is silent for some or all sounds can still be zipped with 'SOUNDS OK' and show a healthy probe line; a package can carry yesterday's sounds after a recording was replaced. Only a person reading the stream measurement would notice. A fully missing folder is caught, by name: that part of the guard holds.
fix: pak_sounds.py: require .uasset, .uexp and .ubulk for every named wave, and when the cooked folder is there (package step: /project/ue/repo-release/unreal/MurderInc/Saved/Cooked/Linux/MurderInc/Content/Audio) a .ubulk of more than 100 bytes for each. Preload(): count a wave with Duration <= 0.01 or no audio chunk as missing (NoteMissing), so sndMissing shows it in a Shipping game. content: do the missing-or-older check on the release copy too when it prints CONTENT KEPT. package Shipping: skip the cook only when the cooked folder is newer than every .uasset under Content/Audio (or always cook after a content step). sync.sh: test for Content/Audio/Web before the early return.

title: The sound's clock is only 0.2 to 0.5 % ahead of real time under the gate's own loads; below 1 the stream has holes all the time, and a Shipping session cannot show which side it is on
evidence: Summaries of the final gate on the zip aa7cc478 (box: /project/ue/cloud/lag/<run>/summary.txt): seconds of sound per second of wall clock 1.0078 to 1.0105 on a free GPU, but snd-l20 1.0032, snd-l35 1.0025, snd-cpu6-l35 1.0020, snd-l20-late 1.0041, snd-l20-c12 1.0047. The docs say '1.004 to 1.007 when the machine is busy'. The device hands out 21.33 ms of sound per wait of 21 ms, so it keeps up only while a wait overshoots by less than 0.33 ms on average; the load lines are at 0.28 to 0.29 ms. What happens past that is measured: snd-env-960 (a buffer with no margin) had 20 drop-outs and 610 ms lost in 65 s, and the holes of a cold start are the same thing for half a minute. E3DS's machine has 8 CPU threads and a card a quarter as fast (DECISIONS.md), and every session there is a cold start whose pipeline precompile takes 6 of the 8.
failure: On a machine a little busier than the box under the 34 ms load the mixer falls behind real time and the stream's sound gets 30 to 50 ms holes for as long as that lasts, not only in the first half minute. The Shipping game's probe line has nothing that would show it in an E3DS session's log, so the first sign would be the owner's ear.
fix: (1) Probe line: add the device's pace (FAudioDevice::GetAudioClock() against the wall clock over the probe interval, as MIAudioEngineTests.cpp already reads it), so one E3DS session with the log in the browser console says whether the clock runs fast or slow there. (2) Try a buffer with more slack, launcher only (no cook, no build): SDL_AUDIO_DEVICE_SAMPLE_FRAMES=1028 instead of clearing the variable (21.42 ms of sound per 21 ms wait: 0.42 ms of slack instead of 0.33, about 2 % fast on a free machine), on the load lines and on the cold-start lines that had holes (snd-l20, snd-l35 with a busy desktop, the two busy loops of snd-x9); untested, and the faster clock has to be weighed against what a browser does with it. (3) Correct the 1.004 to 1.007 in BOX.md, AUDIO.md and PROGRESS to the gate's own numbers.

title: Sounds the data names and nothing in the game ever starts (the reel's boombox among them)
evidence: Every sound id of audio_sounds.json and audio.json searched for in the game's source and tables (the ids built by pattern, <gun>_shot, _tail_*, step_*, *_magin/out, counted as used). Never started: boombox (web: a loop at every reel still to be taken, started in phase with the music and stopped when the reel is secured, src/audio/ambience.js:209-225), neon_buzz and steam (emitters, ambience.js:27, 98), m_riser and m_impact (the conductor's rise into a fight, src/audio/conductor.js:174-175), ui_tick (the web game does not play it either), IR_street and IR_shop (reverb responses, not sounds). All seven are imported, cooked and in the pak (pak_sounds.py counts them). AUDIO.md section 8 lists them as open issues; the report's 'not done' list and PROGRESS section 10 do not. The other way round there is none: every id the code and the tables ask for exists (sndMissing=0 in every run, no 'sound missing' line in the Development log, SoundsResolve).
failure: The player cannot find a reel by ear as in the web game, the music has no rise before a fight, the street has no neon or steam. Nothing breaks; the owner should not read 'sound proven' as 'every web sound is in'.
fix: Name the seven in PROGRESS section 10 and in LAUNCH.md's line on the sound. The boombox is the one with a use in play: a 3D loop (world, ref 2.2, roll 1.25 as in the data) at each reel case, stopped by objective:done for that reel, started in phase (it needs finding 1's PlayWhenSilent to stay there).

title: Small differences from the web game and errors in the write-up
evidence: (a) A Goon's 'ready' call is not pitched by the length of its telegraph (web: react.js:189-194, both kinds; here only the Buzzard); Goon grunts and death cries do not use the Goon's own voice pitch (react.js:211-226); a head hit's impact is not played brighter (react.js:151-155). (b) A stem that should be silent stays at 3 to 6 %: the fade stops when a step is under 0.002 (MIAudioDirector.cpp:1007-1012); this is also what keeps a faded-out stem from being stopped by the engine today, so it must be looked at together with finding 1. (c) UMIFrontEnd::Move plays the hover sound before it knows whether the focus moved. (d) audio.json options.about still says the volume setting is the device's volume after the master chain; the code (MIGameSubsystem.cpp:797-808) and AUDIO.md 3.3 say it is the mix's master trim before it. (e) Gen/bleep_1k.wav is not among the waves Preload keeps in memory (the bleep mode is off). (f) PROGRESS section 4, row 'Steps': the Development run's step_asphalt_run finds are mostly Goon steps, not the demo's walks. (g) The Shipping game's proof of enemies, hits, blasts, reels, stings and Rule's lines in play is its counter only: those kinds were matched in the Development game's recording (the table says D, the summary says both games).
failure: None that a player would report; the list is for whoever next touches the sound.
fix: Fix (a) to (e) with the build of findings 1 and 2 if time allows; correct (d), (f) and (g) in the docs.
